questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
options: I haven't got any left!
I can't remember it!
I can't believe it!
I'm not coming back!
questions.explanation: You heard « je n'en reviens pas », an idiom of astonishment. Taken literally it is 'I'm not coming back from it', which is the trap.

audio.text: Je n'en reviens pas !

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what was said.
options: I'm waiting for you
I'm counting on you
I'll tell you about it
I'm thinking of you
questions.explanation: You heard « je compte sur toi ». « Compter sur » means to rely on; « raconter », which sounds similar, would mean to tell.

audio.text: Je compte sur toi.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the meaning.
options: I've changed my mind about you
I completely agree with you
I completely disagree with you
I'd like to hear your opinion
questions.explanation: You heard « je suis tout à fait de ton avis », 'I'm entirely of your opinion'. It is a useful way to agree in a discussion.

audio.text: Je suis tout à fait de ton avis.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker mean?
options: Don't do that, it will break
Don't go, it will only get worse
Don't bother, it's already arranged
Don't worry, it will work out
questions.explanation: You heard « ne t'en fais pas, ça va s'arranger ». « S'en faire » means to worry, and « s'arranger » here means to sort itself out.

audio.text: Ne t'en fais pas, ça va s'arranger.

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
options: I have just caught my plane
I nearly missed my plane
I missed my plane
I made my plane with time to spare
questions.explanation: You heard « j'ai failli rater mon avion ». « Faillir » plus an infinitive means 'nearly' did something, so the plane was not missed.

audio.text: J'ai failli rater mon avion.

questions.stem: Listen carefully. What does the sentence mean?
options: She works beautifully and follows the rules
She has stopped working and fallen behind
However hard she works, she can't keep up
She works well, so she keeps up easily
questions.explanation: You heard « elle a beau travailler, elle n'arrive pas à suivre ». « Avoir beau » plus an infinitive means 'however much', and has nothing to do with beauty.

audio.text: Elle a beau travailler, elle n'arrive pas à suivre.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker saying?
options: It's a social issue
He is dealing with a social issue
It's a problem that will pass
It's a problem for the school
questions.explanation: You heard « il s'agit d'un problème de société ». « Il s'agit de » is impersonal, 'it is a matter of', so there is no 'he' in the sentence.

audio.text: Il s'agit d'un problème de société.

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what was said.
options: He would rather wait
It's worth the wait
It would be better to wait
It was better to wait
questions.explanation: You heard « il vaudrait mieux attendre », with the conditional « vaudrait ». The « il » is impersonal, so it cannot mean 'he would rather'.

audio.text: Il vaudrait mieux attendre.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the meaning.
options: I admitted I was right
I made up for being wrong
I forgot that I was wrong
I realised I was wrong
questions.explanation: You heard « je me suis rendu compte que j'avais tort ». « Se rendre compte » means to realise, and « avoir tort » is to be wrong.

audio.text: Je me suis rendu compte que j'avais tort.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?
options: You will know the truth soon
You need to know the truth
You must tell the truth
You knew the truth all along
questions.explanation: You heard « il faut que tu saches la vérité », with « saches », the subjunctive of « savoir », after « il faut que ». Telling the truth would be « dire ».

audio.text: Il faut que tu saches la vérité.

questions.stem: Listen carefully. What does the sentence mean?
options: She was finishing just as I arrived
She had already finished when I arrived
She has already finished, and I have arrived
She will have finished by the time I arrive
questions.explanation: You heard « elle avait déjà fini quand je suis arrivé ». The pluperfect « avait fini » puts her finishing before the arrival, both in the past.

audio.text: Elle avait déjà fini quand je suis arrivé.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker asking?
options: Call me because you have received the letter
I will call you when the letter arrives
Call me as soon as you have received the letter
You called me as soon as you got the letter
questions.explanation: You heard « dès que tu auras reçu la lettre, appelle-moi »: a future perfect after « dès que » and an imperative. The speaker is the one waiting for the call.

audio.text: Dès que tu auras reçu la lettre, appelle-moi.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the meaning.
options: I'll make sure you pay attention
I'd like you to be careful
I'd like to be careful myself
I wanted you to pay me back
questions.explanation: You heard « je voudrais que tu fasses attention »: a wish about someone else, so the subjunctive « fasses » follows. « Faire attention » means to be careful.

audio.text: Je voudrais que tu fasses attention.

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what was said.
options: I'm sure it isn't a good idea
I'm not sure it's a good idea
I'm sure it's a good idea
I'm not sure it was a good idea
questions.explanation: You heard « je ne suis pas sûr que ce soit une bonne idée ». Doubt brings the subjunctive « soit », which here is present, not past.

audio.text: Je ne suis pas sûr que ce soit une bonne idée.

questions.stem: Listen carefully. Which did you hear?
options: Nous sommes partis
Nous étions partis
Nous serions partis
Nous serons partis
questions.explanation: You heard the conditional perfect « nous serions partis », 'we would have left'. The future perfect « serons » lacks the « -i- » glide you hear in « serions ».

audio.text: Nous serions partis.

questions.stem: Listen closely. Which was said?
options: Il faut qu'elle tienne
Il faut qu'elle revienne
Il faut qu'elle vienne
Il faut qu'elle devienne
questions.explanation: You heard « il faut qu'elle revienne », 'she has to come back'. The extra syllable « re- » is the only difference from « vienne ».

audio.text: Il faut qu'elle revienne.

questions.stem: Listen. What time is the appointment?
questions.explanation: You heard « quinze heures trente », which on the 24-hour clock is 3.30 pm. « Quinze » is fifteen; 5.30 pm would be « dix-sept heures trente ».

audio.text: Le rendez-vous est fixé à quinze heures trente.

questions.stem: Listen. How much does the ticket cost?
options: 75 euros, with the discount included
65 euros, with the discount included
75 euros, before the discount
95 euros, with the discount included
questions.explanation: You heard « soixante-quinze euros, réduction comprise ». French builds 75 as sixty-fifteen, and « comprise » means the discount is already included.

audio.text: Le billet coûte soixante-quinze euros, réduction comprise.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's attitude to the change?
options: amusement
strong disapproval
cautious approval
complete indifference
questions.explanation: You heard « franchement, je trouve inadmissible qu'on supprime les bus du soir ». « Inadmissible » means unacceptable, and « franchement » adds force.

audio.text: Franchement, je trouve inadmissible qu'on supprime les bus du soir.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker tell their friend?
options: They will help this weekend once their homework is done
They want help with their homework
They're willing to help, but not this weekend
They refuse to help at all
questions.explanation: You heard « je veux bien t'aider, mais pas ce week-end : j'ai trop de devoirs ». « Je veux bien » expresses willingness, and « mais pas ce week-end » limits it.

audio.text: Je veux bien t'aider, mais pas ce week-end : j'ai trop de devoirs.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker doing?
options: raising a concern without rejecting the idea
agreeing with the idea completely
rejecting the idea outright and changing the subject
offering to pay for the idea
questions.explanation: You heard « je ne dis pas que tu as tort, mais as-tu pensé à ce que ça coûterait ? ». The speaker avoids contradicting the other person and raises the cost as a question, a tactful negotiation move.

audio.text: Je ne dis pas que tu as tort, mais as-tu pensé à ce que ça coûterait ?

questions.stem: Listen to the parent. What has been agreed?
options: The party is not allowed, but the teen may go out until midnight
The party is fine, and the parent will pick the teen up at midnight
The party is fine if the teen is home by midnight and texts on arrival
The party is fine as long as the teen texts at midnight to say where they are
questions.explanation: You heard « d'accord pour la soirée, à condition que tu rentres avant minuit et que tu m'envoies un message en arrivant ». « À condition que » sets two conditions, and « en arrivant » means on arriving.

audio.text: Bon, d'accord pour la soirée, à condition que tu rentres avant minuit et que tu m'envoies un message en arrivant.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker propose?
options: cancelling the trip
sharing the petrol costs
taking the train instead
paying for everyone's petrol
questions.explanation: You heard « et si on partageait les frais d'essence ? ». « Si » plus the imperfect makes a suggestion, and « tout le monde y gagne » says everyone benefits.

audio.text: Et si on partageait les frais d'essence ? Comme ça, tout le monde y gagne.

questions.stem: Listen. Which two moves does the speaker make?
options: agrees with the other view, then confirms the final deal
asks for clarification, then offers a compromise
acknowledges the other view, then returns to an open issue
rejects the other view, then changes the subject entirely
questions.explanation: You heard « je comprends ton point de vue, mais revenons à la question du budget ». The first half acknowledges, and « revenons à » revisits something unresolved, both strategies of the Unit 3 role-play.

audio.text: Je comprends ton point de vue, mais revenons à la question du budget.

questions.stem: Listen. Who is the speaker most likely talking to?
options: a younger brother at home
a classmate in the playground
an interviewer at the end of a meeting
a close friend at the end of a long party
questions.explanation: You heard « je vous remercie de m'avoir reçu », a formal thank-you using « vous » for being seen or received. The other situations would call for « tu ».

audio.text: Je vous remercie de m'avoir reçu.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker asking?
options: for the music to be turned down
for the music to be turned up
whether the music can be heard
who chose this music
questions.explanation: You heard « tu pourrais baisser la musique, s'il te plaît ? ». « Baisser » means to lower, and the conditional « pourrais » makes the request polite.

audio.text: Tu pourrais baisser la musique, s'il te plaît ?

questions.stem: Listen to the examiner's question. What are you being asked?
options: Why did we choose this topic for you?
Could you choose a different topic?
Could you explain why you chose this topic?
Could you explain this topic to us?
questions.explanation: You heard « pourriez-vous nous expliquer pourquoi vous avez choisi ce sujet ? ». « Pourquoi » asks for your reasons, not for an explanation of the topic itself.

audio.text: Pourriez-vous nous expliquer pourquoi vous avez choisi ce sujet ?

questions.stem: Listen to the English, then choose the French.
options: J'apprends le français pendant six ans
J'apprendrai le français pour six ans
J'apprends le français depuis six ans
J'ai appris le français il y a six ans
questions.explanation: 'I've been learning French for six years' is still true now, so French uses the present with « depuis ». « Il y a six ans » would mean six years ago.

audio.text: I've been learning French for six years.

questions.stem: Listen to the English and choose the French.
options: J'aurai aimé rester plus longtemps
J'aurais aimé rester plus longtemps
J'aimerais rester plus longtemps
J'avais aimé rester plus longtemps
questions.explanation: 'Would have liked' is the conditional perfect, « j'aurais aimé ». « J'aurai aimé », without the s, is the future perfect: it sounds almost the same but means 'will have liked'.

audio.text: I would have liked to stay longer.

questions.stem: Listen to the English, then choose the French for it.
options: C'est le plus bon film que j'aie jamais vu
C'est le meilleur film qui j'aie jamais vu
C'est le meilleur film que j'aie jamais vu
C'est le mieux film que j'aie jamais vu
questions.explanation: 'Best' with a noun is « le meilleur », the superlative of « bon »; « plus bon » does not exist and « mieux » is an adverb. The film is the object of « vu », so the relative is « que ».

audio.text: It's the best film I have ever seen.

questions.stem: Listen to the English and choose the French.
options: On en reparlait plus tard
On en reparlera plus tard
On y reparlera plus tard
On le reparlera plus tard
questions.explanation: 'Talk about it again' is « reparler de », so 'about it' becomes « en ». « Reparlait » is the imperfect, which would put it in the past.

audio.text: We'll talk about it again later.

questions.stem: Listen to the English, then choose the matching French idiom.
options: Tournons la page
Cassons-nous la tête
Coupons la poire en deux
Mettons les points sur les i
questions.explanation: 'Let's split the difference' is « coupons la poire en deux », a compromise in a negotiation. « Mettre les points sur les i » means to spell things out, and « tourner la page » means to move on.

audio.text: Let's split the difference.

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
options: It hurts me when you look at me
It's not worth seeing you like this
It makes me laugh to see you like this
It upsets me to see you like this
questions.explanation: You heard « ça me fait de la peine de te voir comme ça ». « Faire de la peine à quelqu'un » is to upset or sadden them; it is about feelings, not physical pain.

audio.text: Ça me fait de la peine de te voir comme ça.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the meaning.
options: What a pity he can't come with us
Never mind, he'll do it without us
Too bad, we'll manage without him
Fine, we'll wait for him
questions.explanation: You heard « tant pis, on fera sans lui ». « Tant pis » shrugs off a setback, and « on fera sans lui » means 'we'll do without him'.

audio.text: Tant pis, on fera sans lui.

questions.stem: Listen carefully. What does the sentence mean?
options: If you had come, you would have had a great time
If you come, you will have a great time
If you came, you would have a great time
When you came, you had a great time
questions.explanation: You heard « si tu étais venu, tu te serais bien amusé »: pluperfect after « si », then the conditional perfect of a pronominal verb, with « être ». It is about a missed past chance.

audio.text: Si tu étais venu, tu te serais bien amusé.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?
options: It looks like it's going to rain
They say it rained yesterday
It has just started raining
It won't rain today after all
questions.explanation: You heard « on dirait qu'il va pleuvoir ». « On dirait que » means 'it looks as if', and « va pleuvoir » is the near future.

audio.text: On dirait qu'il va pleuvoir.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the meaning.
options: Whatever the case, a decision has to be made
Whoever he is, he has to make a decision
Although it is late, he has made a decision
Whenever it suits, we can decide later
questions.explanation: You heard « quoi qu'il en soit, il faut prendre une décision ». « Quoi qu'il en soit » means 'be that as it may', with the subjunctive « soit », and « il » is impersonal.

audio.text: Quoi qu'il en soit, il faut prendre une décision.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker think?
options: I was surprised that he came
It surprised him that I came
I'm sure that he will come
I'd be surprised if he came
questions.explanation: You heard « ça m'étonnerait qu'il vienne ». The conditional « étonnerait » with the subjunctive « vienne » expresses doubt: the speaker does not expect him.

audio.text: Ça m'étonnerait qu'il vienne.

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement. What is happening on the metro?
options: Line 4 is stopped by a technical fault
Line 4 will close at four o'clock today
Line 4 is running four minutes late
Line 4 has reopened after technical work
questions.explanation: You heard « suite à un incident technique, le trafic est interrompu sur la ligne quatre ». « Interrompu » means stopped, and « suite à » means following or because of.

audio.text: Suite à un incident technique, le trafic est interrompu sur la ligne quatre du métro.

questions.stem: Listen. How many people took part last year?
questions.explanation: You heard « quatre-vingt-onze », four-twenty-eleven: 80 + 11 = 91. 71 is « soixante et onze », and 81 is « quatre-vingt-un ».

audio.text: Il y avait quatre-vingt-onze participants l'année dernière.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker saying?
options: The more I think about it, the more convinced I am
The less I think about it, the more convinced I am
I'm thinking about it less now that I'm convinced
The more I think about it, the less convinced I am
questions.explanation: You heard « plus j'y pense, moins je suis convaincue ». « Plus… moins » sets up 'the more… the less'; « y » stands for the thing being thought about.

audio.text: Plus j'y pense, moins je suis convaincue.
